Contributing to MarkFlowy

Welcome, and thank you for your interest in contributing to MarkFlowy!

How to Contribute Code

Prerequisites

In order to download necessary tools, clone the repository, and install dependencies via yarn, you need network access.

You'll need the following tools:

  • Git
  • Node.js 24, as declared in .node-version.
  • Yarn 4.8.0, selected by the root packageManager field through Corepack.
  • Rust 1.96, selected by rust-toolchain.toml through rustup.
  • The Tauri platform prerequisites for your operating system.

Table of Contents

  • Contributing to MarkFlowy
    • How to Contribute Code
      • Prerequisites
      • Table of Contents
      • Contribute multilingual translations steps
        • Fork
        • Translation file
      • Development work steps
        • Fork
        • Dependency installation
        • Startup MarkFlowy
  • Thank You!

Contribute multilingual translations steps

For some users who don't want to go through the complicated project startup steps and just want to participate in the translation work, you can check the following steps.

Fork

Fork MarkFlowy and git clone

Translation file

Add a new language

Desktop translations live in the root locales directory; shared editor translations are in locales/editor, and website translations in locales/web. Start from the English resource for the relevant surface. A new language also needs registration in that surface's locale list. Run yarn translate:check after editing translations; this check does not require the private runtime.

Modify an existing language

Modifying the existing language may not be particularly easy to find the corresponding key. If you do not find it in the locales file, you can mention the issue, and I will help you find the corresponding place to modify.

Development work steps

Fork

Fork MarkFlowy and git clone

Dependency installation

Execute the following command to install related dependencies.

corepack enable
yarn install --immutable

No GitHub Packages token is needed for the public dependency install. Keep the tracked lockfile and the dependency source patches applied by postinstall.

Startup MarkFlowy

Prepare Desktop's workspace dependencies once, then start the development runner:

yarn turbo run build --filter='@markflowy/desktop^...' --concurrency=2
yarn dev:desktop

The runner checks the Rust toolchain, starts dependency watchers, waits for their outputs and launches Tauri. It compiles development code; the commands above are setup instructions, not evidence that a native build has been validated for a particular change. You do not need cargo install to launch this checkout.

Public checkout and private editor runtime

Capricorn is currently not open source. Its source repository and runtime package are private and are not included in MarkFlowy's public repository. The public checkout supports Markdown source and reading modes without Capricorn. Live editing requires the private package @drl990114/capricorn-runtime, whose manifest is marked UNLICENSED. RME and its ProseMirror/CodeMirror integration remain in packages/editor.

Maintainers with package access can provide GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN or NODE_AUTH_TOKEN through their local environment or ignored root .env, then run:

yarn install:capricorn-runtime

The installer uses the exact version and tarball SHA-256 pinned in scripts/install-capricorn-runtime.mjs, writes to the ignored .private-runtime directory, and validates package identity. Restart the development server after installation. Do not commit tokens, runtime files or generated declarations. Fork pull requests do not receive the private package credential.

Validation before a pull request

Public contributors can run focused tests for the changed behavior and Desktop's build:types script (tsc --noEmit, covering both src and tests) without access to Capricorn. RME still powers source mode, preview and export, so its tests remain in packages/editor.

Maintainers with access to the private runtime run test:capricorn-published to check MarkFlowy's integration with the pinned package. This suite and the regular test suite are disjoint; CI runs each once, and the runtime suite remains a required release gate. A public checkout's fallback cannot establish parity with the private runtime.

test:capricorn-source is for maintainers who also have access to Capricorn's private source repository and a local checkout. Package access alone does not grant source access. It runs the same host contracts against that checkout for local integration work. Editor-internal regressions are maintained and tested in Capricorn's private repository; public contributors do not need to obtain its source or run these private checks themselves.

yarn workspace @markflowy/desktop build:types
yarn workspace @markflowy/desktop test <path-to-test>
# Maintainers with private package access and the pinned runtime installed:
yarn workspace @markflowy/desktop test:capricorn-published

For changed TypeScript files, use the existing ESLint 8 runner without --fix:

node node_modules/@umijs/fabric/node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js \
  --resolve-plugins-relative-to node_modules/@umijs/fabric <changed-files>

Run affected Rust unit tests when native code changes. Record which checks passed and which native scenarios were not exercised; unit tests do not verify OS input methods, installer signing or upgrade behavior.

How to Submit Themes to the Theme Store

MarkFlowy has a built-in theme store feature where users can browse, download, and install community-created themes. If you want to submit your own theme to the theme store for other users, please refer to the "Sharing Your Theme" section in the Custom Theme Documentation, which details the complete process for theme creation and submission to the theme store.

Thank You!

Your contributions to open source, large or small, make the project better. Thank you for taking the time to contribute.

hero.title: MarkFlowy
hero.subtitle: A local-first Markdown editor focused on large documents and optional AI.
hero.description: Find your writing flow with MarkFlowy, a local-first Markdown editor for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Visual and source editing, with optional AI assistance.

features.lead: A minimalist yet powerful editor that combines AI intelligence with refined writing experience — built for those who value focus and craft.

feature1.title: Multiple Editing Modes
feature1.description: Supports source code and WYSIWYG editing modes to meet different scenario needs, and supports editing files other than Markdown, such as JSON, TXT, etc.

feature2.title: Built-in AI Assistant
feature2.description: Integrates a powerful AI assistant that supports text generation, conversation, translation, and other functions to improve editing efficiency.

feature3.title: Custom Themes
feature3.description: Provides built-in light and dark themes, and supports custom themes to meet personalized needs.

capability1.title: WYSIWYG & Source Code
capability1.body: Seamlessly switch between What You See Is What You Get and source code modes. Edit Markdown, JSON, TXT and more with full flexibility.

capability2.title: Copilot & Smart Assist
capability2.body: Connect optional AI providers for chat, translation, summaries, and Copilot. Choose cloud services or run a local model with Ollama.

capability3.title: Large-document editing
capability3.body: Optimized loading and rendering make large Markdown documents smoother to open, scroll through, and edit.

capability4.title: Themes & Hotkeys
capability4.body: Design your own editor themes and share them. Fully customizable keyboard shortcuts to match your workflow.

hero.title: Your ideas, in full flow.
hero.lead: A Markdown editor crafted for smooth editing and focused writing.
hero.description: Local-first, with visual and source editing. Your AI assistant can use the official Skill to open, save, and export documents in MarkFlowy.
hero.platforms: Made for the way you work

preview.title: A folder for everything taking shape.
preview.description: Open a local folder to bring notes, drafts, and project files together. Browse your files, follow the document outline, and keep writing in the same window.
preview.screenshotAlt: MarkFlowy desktop in light mode, showing local files, the visual editor, and document outline

singleFile.title: One file. Your full attention.
singleFile.description: Open a Markdown file and start writing. No workspace setup required, with the same editor tools ready when you need them.

open.title: Open a file and begin
open.body: Work directly with a local document, or start a new note and save it where it belongs.

focus.title: Keep the page quiet
focus.body: A compact title bar leaves room for your words. Click the document name to rename it.

grow.title: Add a folder when you need one
grow.body: Open a local folder when one note becomes a project. Your familiar writing tools come with you.

singleFile.screenshotAlt: MarkFlowy Desktop in single-file mode, with a Markdown document and its filename in the compact title bar

features.title: Everything your writing needs. Nothing in its way.
features.description: From a quick note to a long document, build a writing flow that feels like your own.

write.title: Markdown, the way you think.
write.body: Write visually or get closer to the source. Work with Markdown, JSON, and plain text in one familiar space.
write.alt: MarkFlowy desktop editor displaying a writing sample

local.title: High performance for longer drafts.
local.body: Optimized loading and rendering make large documents smoother to open, scroll through, and edit. Work directly with files in your own folders.

ai.title: A little help, when you need it.
ai.body: Bring your own AI service for conversations, summaries, and translation, or connect a local model with Ollama.
ai.alt: MarkFlowy desktop editor with its optional AI assistant panel

personal.title: Make yourself at home.
personal.body: Choose your theme, set your shortcuts, and settle into a distraction-free space that works for you.

workflow.title: One space. Your whole writing flow.

capture.title: Catch the thought.
capture.body: Open a single file for a quick thought, or a folder for a larger project. Start writing without importing your notes.

refine.title: Find the right words.
refine.body: Use headings and the outline to shape your draft. Switch between visual and source editing, with optional AI for summaries and translation.

share.title: Take it with you.
share.body: Keep your Markdown files, export HTML or an image, or save a PDF through the system print dialog. Take your writing wherever it needs to go.

stats.eyebrow: Built in the open, growing together
stats.title: Small contributions. Lasting progress.
stats.body: A star, a download, a contribution. MarkFlowy grows with people who care about writing and open source.
stats.downloadNote: Downloads include stable installers and update packages.

community.title: Better, together.
community.body: MarkFlowy grows with the people who use it. Read the code, share an idea, report a bug, or help shape what comes next.

cta.title: Your next idea starts here.
cta.body: A little more focus. A lot more flow.

footer.made: Made for the love of writing.
